previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with multiple myeloma, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease, was admitted for influenza with symptoms of cough, fatigue, and fever. He was started on renally dosed Tamiflu and monitored closely. Due to symptomatic anemia with hemoglobin of 7.0 g/dL, he received one unit of packed red blood cells, with improvement to 7.8 g/dL. His chronic leg edema was managed with continuation of torsemide and initiation of metolazone 5 mg daily, to be taken half an hour prior to torsemide. His home medications, including insulin, acyclovir, prednisone, and allopurinol, were continued. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with instructions to complete the Tamiflu course, monitor daily weights, follow a low-salt diet, and follow up with oncology for management of myeloma and pancytopenia.
